import math

def best_average(a: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    # Prefix sums: P[i] = sum(a[0...i-1])
    # Subarray sum from i to j (0 <= i <= j - k <= n - k) is P[j] - P[i], length is j - i.
    # Geometrically, points (i, P[i]) in 2D. We want to maximize the slope of the line
    # passing through (i, P[i]) and (j, P[j]) with j - i >= k.
    # This is a classic problem solvable in O(n) using a lower convex hull.
    
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        P[i + 1] = P[i] + a[i]
        
    # We maintain the lower convex hull of points (i, P[i]) in a deque / list.
    # When considering right endpoint j (from k to n), the candidate left endpoints i <= j - k
    # are added to the hull.
    # Since x-coordinates are increasing, we can maintain the hull.
    # To find the maximum slope from (j, P[j]) to points on the hull,
    # the slope is maximized at a tangent point. As j increases, the optimal tangent point
    # on the lower convex hull also moves monotonically to the right.
    
    hull = []
    
    def cross_product(p1, p2, p3):
        # (p2.x - p1.x)*(p3.y - p1.y) - (p2.y - p1.y)*(p3.x - p1.x)
        # > 0 means counter-clockwise turn
        # <= 0 means clockwise or collinear
        return (p2[0] - p1[0]) * (p3[1] - p1[1]) - (p2[1] - p1[1]) * (p3[0] - p1[0])

    best_p = -1
    best_q = 1
    
    head = 0
    for j in range(k, n + 1):
        # Add new candidate left endpoint: i = j - k
        new_pt = (j - k, P[j - k])
        while len(hull) - head >= 2:
            if cross_product(hull[-2], hull[-1], new_pt) <= 0:
                hull.pop()
            else:
                break
        hull.append(new_pt)
        
        # Now find the point in hull[head:] that maximizes the slope to (j, P[j])
        cur_pt = (j, P[j])
        while len(hull) - head >= 2:
            # Compare slope between hull[head] and cur_pt vs hull[head+1] and cur_pt
            # slope(hull[head+1], cur_pt) >= slope(hull[head], cur_pt)
            # iff cross_product(hull[head], hull[head+1], cur_pt) <= 0
            if cross_product(hull[head], hull[head + 1], cur_pt) <= 0:
                head += 1
            else:
                break
                
        opt_i, opt_pi = hull[head]
        p = P[j] - opt_pi
        q = j - opt_i
        
        # Compare with best: p/q > best_p/best_q <=> p * best_q > best_p * q
        if best_p == -1 or p * best_q > best_p * q:
            best_p = p
            best_q = q

    g = math.gcd(best_p, best_q)
    return [best_p // g, best_q // g]
